title: OctetProof witness observation
description: What one witness saw in one golden-artifact input, plus enough provenance to replay it. OctetProof 1.1.0 §6.2 (docs/octetproof-spec.md). Producers: `rvt-ifc --observation PATH --artifact-id ID` (source witness) and `tools/ci/witness-ifcopenshell.py --observation PATH` (bridge witness). Committed instances live under research/witness/<artifact_id>/observations/. Emitting an observation is not a capability claim; only a PASS verdict across independent witnesses is.

schema_version.description: The OctetProof version this observation conforms to. 1.1.0 added the optional `relations` payload key and the `relations` surface term (§20); the envelope is otherwise unchanged, so 1.0.0 observations stay valid (§16.2).

witness_id.description: Registry id (research/witness-registry.json → witnesses[].id). A witness absent from the registry makes the verdict a MANIFEST_ERROR.

witness_version.description: Exact version of the witness that produced this observation (§9.6).

input_role.description: Which side of the recorded edge this witness read. Resolved against the manifest hashes by the gate; a mismatch is REJECTED_INPUT (§10.5).

input_file.description: File name of the input as read.

input_hash_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the input bytes. Must equal the manifest hash for the declared role.

deterministic.description: The witness's attestation for this run (§9.5). Anything but true rejects the witness.

semantic_surface_covered.description: The §9.4 controlled vocabulary this witness claims for this run. A witness is compared only on what it declares; `entity_counts` is required by the reference gate.

observation.description: The payload — the only part that is canonicalized, hashed, and diffed. `entity_counts` and `relations` are the cross-witness surface; every other key is witness-specific and is not compared.

entity_counts.description: Per-type instance counts. A type absent here counts as zero.

relations.description: Per-relation pair multisets (§7.2, added in 1.1.0). Each value is the relation's `[a_identity, b_identity]` pairs sorted lexicographically, duplicates kept. An identity the witness cannot read is the empty string, never an omitted pair. A relation absent here is an empty set.

observation_hash_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the canonicalized `observation` payload (§7.3: sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, UTF-8). Replay compares a fresh run against this value.

unsupported_entities.description: What the witness could not read. Recorded, never a disagreement (§7.1 rule 4).
